archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing-and-rhythm)
archetype.definition: A classic distributor working from structure. Goff wins with timing, play-action and placement from the pocket, not with his legs, and this year he is pairing that with a more aggressive downfield lean than he has shown since his rookie season.

report.headline: Best per-game EPA in football, driven by a new appetite for the intermediate middle
report.take:
Goff is the same quarterback he has been for a decade: a pocket passer who throws on time, lives off play design and has never been a runner. He has 16 rushing yards and a -0.389 EPA per carry, and that's fine. What has changed is where the ball goes. His aggressiveness (throws into tight windows) has jumped to 19.37% from 12.5% last year, and his intended air yards sit at 8.45, well above the 6.8 aDOT of his last two seasons. The result is 0.323 EPA per dropback, fifth among 45 qualifiers, and a per-game passing EPA that ranks first.

The engine is the 10-19 yard window. On 47 intermediate attempts he is at 0.965 EPA a throw, and those plays account for 45.3 EPA, most of his dropback value. His 10-plus air-yard throws as a group run at 1.03 EPA, against 0.114 on everything under 10. Sam LaPorta (0.854 EPA per target) and Jameson Williams (0.705) are the ones cashing it. Amon-Ra St. Brown has drawn the most targets at 57 but sits at a modest 0.189 a target. Some of that is volume regressing toward short, high-percentage work. Some of it is that the offense is leaning on the vertical and seam stuff right now.

The numbers flatter him in a few ways. The schedule has been soft: four of five opponents rank 19th or worse in defensive EPA today. The one top-half defense, the Jets (11th), still got a 6.9 CPOE, 12.1-EPA game out of him, which is the strongest evidence this is real. His own defense ranks dead last in EPA allowed, so every game has gone over the total and he has had 64 dropbacks trailing by 9+. That inflates attempts and yardage. Zero interceptions is the shakiest piece: his bad-throw rate ranks 28th of 37, he has four turnover-worthy fumbles with none lost, and he is throwing into tighter windows than ever. His career has never gone long without picks.

Where it heads: the efficiency should cool toward his 2024 level rather than stay on a 41-touchdown, zero-interception pace. The volume floor is sturdy, because Detroit's defense guarantees shootouts. Third down is the one genuine soft spot to fix, at -0.034 EPA with a 36.7% conversion rate and a -10.1 CPOE.

strengths.title: Intermediate and downfield efficiency
strengths.body: His 10-19 yard throws are producing close to a point of EPA apiece, and that window holds most of his passing value. It rests on scheme and on LaPorta and Williams winning between the numbers, so the core should last. The 15-attempt deep split at 1.232 EPA is a hint, not a baseline.

strengths.title: More aggressive without losing efficiency
strengths.body: He is attacking tight windows far more than last year and pushing intended air yards up, yet his completion rate and CPOE are nearly unchanged. That suggests the throws are coming within structure, with play design manufacturing the windows, rather than from forcing. It looks like a deliberate offensive choice, so expect it to persist.

strengths.title: Shootout volume baked in
strengths.body: Detroit's defense ranks last in EPA allowed, so Goff keeps throwing into the fourth quarter, and he has been efficient doing it from behind. That keeps his yardage and attempts high regardless of opponent, and it won't change unless the defense does.

concerns.title: Zero interceptions won't hold
concerns.body: A clean interception sheet combined with a bottom-third bad-throw rate and four turnover-worthy fumbles points to luck. His career has run 7-16 picks a year, and he is throwing into more tight windows now. Expect picks to arrive, though more as an occasional cost than a collapse.

concerns.title: Third down is a weak spot
concerns.body: On third down he is below average in EPA, with a big negative CPOE, on an average of 7.7 yards to go. Long-yardage downs take away the play-action and early-down design he thrives on. It is a modest sample, but it fits his long-standing profile as a quarterback who is best on schedule.

concerns.title: Soft schedule and sack conversion
concerns.body: Most of his production has come against defenses ranked 19th or worse. He also turns pressure into sacks at a below-median rate, which is a trait he has carried for years. With guard Ben Bartch (93% of snaps) now on IR, a better front could test that.

trend.note: After a modest Week 1 (5.9 EPA), he has posted 12+ passing EPA in four straight games. The last three run slightly above his season in EPA per dropback (+0.017) and yards per attempt (+0.58).

nextGame.headline: Strength meets strength: Green Bay erases explosive passes
nextGame.body:
Green Bay is the first pass defense on his schedule built to blunt exactly what is working. The Packers rank 8th in pass EPA allowed and 1st in explosive pass rate allowed, and they hold quarterbacks to 12.1 PPR a game, 5th-fewest. Goff's season leans on chunk throws in the 10-plus window, and this unit is designed to keep everything in front of it. That points to a longer, more methodical day built on completions underneath and third-down conversions, his weakest area. The counterweight is the Packers' run defense, 27th in EPA. Detroit can lean on the ground game and play-action to manufacture the intermediate windows, and the game is indoors after a bye with a 53.5 total.

Availability tilts slightly his way. Micah Parsons remains out, though he hasn't played all season, so the Packers' numbers already reflect his absence. The new losses are inside: DTs Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford went to IR, and Jordon Riley is out. That thins interior pressure right where Detroit is patching a line without Bartch and possibly still without center Cade Mays. Starting corner Brandon Cisse (88% of snaps) is questionable with a stinger, and if he sits, the secondary's discipline takes a real hit.

keyMatchups.title: Chunk throws vs a no-explosives defense
keyMatchups.body: Goff's value has come from throws of 10-plus air yards, and Green Bay allows the fewest explosive passes in the league. If the Packers keep the lid on, his EPA per attempt will fall back toward his under-10 level. In that case his production depends on volume.

keyMatchups.title: LaPorta against a stingy TE defense
keyMatchups.body: LaPorta has been Goff's most efficient target by a wide margin. Green Bay holds top tight ends below their averages and sees a smaller-than-normal share of targets go to the position. St. Brown in the WR1 role may be the easier lane, since that is where the Packers have given up the most over average.

keyMatchups.title: Game script: Packers can't run
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay's offense ranks last in rush EPA, so it will have to throw to keep pace. That favors a higher-scoring, pass-heavy game against a Lions defense that has allowed shootouts every week. Meanwhile, Detroit can run on the Packers' 27th-ranked run defense to set up play-action.

nextGame.watch: Whether Goff can keep finding the intermediate middle for LaPorta and Williams against a defense that refuses explosives, or whether he gets pushed into third-and-long, where he has struggled.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sustainable. He has a top-three offense, a pass-catching group that wins between the numbers, and a defense so porous that he will keep throwing late in games. Expect high attempts and yardage to continue, and his efficiency to stay top-ten. A run of near-1.0 EPA intermediate throws should cool as better defenses appear, and Green Bay, along with other top-half units, will test that.

The parts to discount are the zero interceptions and the 41-touchdown pace. With his aggressiveness up and his bad-throw rate in the bottom third, interceptions should show up at something like his career norm. Touchdowns should settle around two a game rather than above it. Pressure-to-sack conversion is the swing to watch while the interior line is patched.
swingFactors: Interior line health (Bartch IR, Mays return)
Whether the intermediate/deep efficiency survives tougher pass defenses
Lions defense keeping games in shootout mode

confidence.note: Five games against mostly weak defenses, but the passing profile matches his strong 2024 and the approach change looks schematic.
